paragraphs.text: Because the Jews thought themselves so strong by reason of this mountain, that no enemy could come to hurt them, the Prophet shows that when God sends the enemies, it will show itself ready to receive them.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: Showing that if the strong men were destroyed, the weaker were not able to resist.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: Seeing that Lebanon was destroyed, which was the strongest fortress, the weaker places could not hope to hold out.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: That is, the fame of Judah and Israel would perish.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: Which being now destined to be slain, were delivered as out of the lion's mouth.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: Their governors destroy them without any remorse of conscience, or yet thinking that they do evil.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: He notes the hypocrites, who always have the name of God in their mouths, though in their life and doings they deny God, attributing their gain to God's blessings, which comes from the wealth of their brethren.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: I will cause one to destroy another.
paragraphs.label: h
paragraphs.anchor: I will deliver the men every

paragraphs.text: Their governors will execute cruelty over them.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: That is, the small remnant, whom he though worthy to show mercy to.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: God shows his great benefits toward his people to convince them of greater ingratitude, who would neither be ruled by his most beautiful order of government, neither continue in the bands of brotherly unity, and therefore he breaks both the one and the other. Some read "Destroyers" instead of "Bands", but in Zec 11:14 the second reading is confirmed.
paragraphs.label: l

paragraphs.text: By which he shows his care and diligence that he would not allow them to have evil rulers, so that they would consider his great love.
paragraphs.label: m
paragraphs.anchor: Three shepherds also I cut off

paragraphs.text: Meaning, the people, because they would not acknowledge these great benefits of God.
paragraphs.label: n

paragraphs.text: He shows that the least always profit by God's judgments.
paragraphs.label: o
paragraphs.anchor: poor of the flock that waited

paragraphs.text: Besides their ingratitude, God accuses them of malice and wickedness, who did not only forget his benefits, but esteemed them as nothing.
paragraphs.label: p

paragraphs.text: Showing that it was too little to pay his wages with, which could hardly suffice to make a few tiles to cover the temple.
paragraphs.label: q

paragraphs.text: Signifying that they should have a certain type of regiment and outward show of government: but in effect it would be nothing, for they would be wolves, and devouring beasts instead of shepherds.
paragraphs.label: r
paragraphs.anchor: the instruments of a foolish shepherd

paragraphs.text: And is in health and sound.
paragraphs.label: s

paragraphs.text: By the arm he signifies strength, as he does wisdom and judgments by the eye: that is, the plague of God will take away both your strength and judgment.
paragraphs.label: t
